general_information.Description: * This course is designed to introduce students to significant features of cultural, social, political, and artistic life in modern Britain and different aspects of American cultural and socio-political life such as the American Dream & American identity, race, immigration, religion, and the global transmission of American culture. Students will develop a broader and deeper understanding of various aspects of British and American culture. * The course integrates a range of scholarly texts and up-to-date multimedia materials, allowing students to engage critically with key theoretical concepts and their contemporary evolutions in current events. * Learning takes place through active class participation, independent study, project-based assignments, group presentations, debates, and creative multimedia tasks (including responsible use of AI tools). * Through this course, students will develop academic reading and writing skills, analytical thinking, cultural awareness, teamwork, and oral communication. Assessment structure: 1) Ongoing assessment - Assignments: 04*15%: 60% (Lecturers wishing to apply PBL may also combine 2 or 3 assignments into 1 project and adjust the weight accordingly) - Group Project Essay: 01*20%: 20% 2) Final Examination (FE) 20% 3) Final Result 100% 4) Completion Criteria: Ongoing assessment >0 & Group Project Essay >=4/10, Final Exam Score >=4/10, Final Result >=5/10.
general_information.StudentTasks: - Attend at least 80% of contact hours in order to be accepted to the final examination - Actively participate in class activities - Fulfil tasks given by instructor before and after class - Use their own laptop in class only for learning purposes

learning_outcomes.CLO Details: Develop a broader and deeper understanding of key aspects of American historical and cultural developments
Develop a broader and deeper understanding of various aspects of social and cultural context in contemporary Britain
Identify and describe major concepts related to national identity, race relations, immigration, gender politics, and cultural transmission in American and British societies
Produce clear, coherent, and well-structured academic essays and oral presentations on a range of topics in English

assessments.Grading Guide: In groups of 3, students write an analytical essay on a specific question given by lecturer based on a contemporary source document (newspaper articles, educational videos, news reports, Ted Talks, etc.) related to one of the topics discussed in the course. The essay must: 1) Address the question & topic by referring to specific examples from the source material, drawing on knowledge of studied topics, and researching additional sources to support the analysis. 2) Use appropriate references in APA style. Word count: 500 words Students submit the essay at the end of the course (the last day). The essay is the source for the final exam. Students must also submit the presentation slides for the final exam on the last day of the course. Lecturers will forward the slides to the Exam Department for the final exam presentation.

constructive_questions.Name: CQ2.1
constructive_questions.Details: Which features of the country USA do you find it more interesting? Explain.

constructive_questions.Name: CQ2.2
constructive_questions.Details: How does Jay Gatsby from the novel by F. Scott Fitzgerald depict an American identity?

constructive_questions.Name: CQ2.3
constructive_questions.Details: Should there be or not have a distinctive American identity? To what consequences can it lead?

constructive_questions.Name: CQ2.4
constructive_questions.Details: Notice the inaugural address of the US presidents, which of them do you think had the most hope for the country and for the American people? Explain. You may also compare and contrast. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Qszv668rN20 – Bill Clinton https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=JwcR00oGbv0 – Barrack Obama https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ThtRvBUBpQ4 – Donald Trump https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Wa9KI4dflY4 - Joe Biden

constructive_questions.Name: CQ3.1
constructive_questions.Details: America as the land of the free; as the land of opportunity: Native Americans, African Americans as well as immigrants from Europe must embrace "Americannes" notion for them to be allowed to migrate to the USA. Do you think it would be worth it to extract your own origin to reach your American dream? Why/why not?

constructive_questions.Name: CQ3.2
constructive_questions.Details: What are some examples of how food, business practices, and advertising have changed because of immigration?

constructive_questions.Name: CQ3.3
constructive_questions.Details: What do you think are some of the economic or social disadvantages of immigration in the USA? Discuss.

constructive_questions.Name: CQ4.1
constructive_questions.Details: Some have argued that hybridity represents the best hope for America as diverse culture. To what extent do you agree or disagree?

constructive_questions.Name: CQ4.2
constructive_questions.Details: Which metaphor do you think American ethnicity best illustrated ; melting pot, mosaic, salad bowl or other illustration? Explain.

constructive_questions.Name: CQ4.3
constructive_questions.Details: How do you think people from the videos survive the migration process? Group 1: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=DTIDCA7mjZs - How to Illegally Cross the Mexico-US Border Group 2: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ZWq0v4ucav0 - Walking to America with the Migrant Caravan Group 3: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=RSwwO00qeB0 - Riding 'The Death Train' to America's border

constructive_questions.Name: CQ5.1
constructive_questions.Details: In God we trust is the official motto of the United States. Also, notice the patriotic songs/national anthem of the USA, have you noticed that most of these songs are related to religion? What can be implied from this notion? IMAGE: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/In_God_We_Trust Group 1: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=HsdMfWJ7pvA - Ariana Grande performing the National Anthem - Star Spangled Banner Group 2: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Se1b3yFTVRU – Godbless America Lady Gaga Group 3: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=XnCNHFg9y1Q – God less the USA Group 4: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=8s2DViOOElA - "This Land Is Your Land" & "America, The Beautiful"

constructive_questions.Name: CQ5.2
constructive_questions.Details: Do you think the U.S. government should interfere with how churches operate?

constructive_questions.Name: CQ5.3
constructive_questions.Details: Do you think that secularization is good for the growth of countries?

constructive_questions.Name: CQ6.1
constructive_questions.Details: Which side do you agree with? Defend your answer. (1) Religion is a must if a politician is running for a position in the US Congress. (2) Using the mass media (TV,RADIO,electronic medium,etc) are good initiatives to propagate evangelism in the US.

constructive_questions.Name: CQ6.2
constructive_questions.Details: How have non-Christian religions such as Judaism and Islam ﬁtted into a society that has tended to assume that America is a Christian nation above all?

constructive_questions.Name: CQ6.3
constructive_questions.Details: Is there an argument that religion is becoming less important in the United States, and that increasing numbers of the young, in particular, are losing any clear religious affiliation? What might this do for the place of Christianity in America?

constructive_questions.Name: CQ7.1
constructive_questions.Details: With your background knowledge, how would you define gender and sexuality in the US? Is it similar to your country Vietnam? To what extent are they similar or different?

constructive_questions.Name: CQ7.2
constructive_questions.Details: How far would you agree that America is a male-dominated and male-defined society? How about your country Vietnam?

constructive_questions.Name: CQ7.3
constructive_questions.Details: Which American movie/TV series would you believe in having a strong feminism/masculism approach? Discuss briefly. Prepare for a role playing about gender inequality. Any setting is accepted.

constructive_questions.Name: CQ8.1
constructive_questions.Details: Discuss the first and second waves of feminism. In what way these movements shape women's rights today?

constructive_questions.Name: CQ8.2
constructive_questions.Details: Sex and the City can be viewed as a “post-feminist” text redeﬁning female identities in complex and varied ways. To what extent do you agree with this idea?

constructive_questions.Name: CQ8.3
constructive_questions.Details: Define the LGBTQ+. What have this group gone through in their fight for legal rights in the US?

constructive_questions.Name: CQ8.4
constructive_questions.Details: How is same sex marriage perceived in Vietnam?

constructive_questions.Name: CQ9.1
constructive_questions.Details: What does "Americanisation" mean? Give examples. What effects has it had on people's lives around the globe?

constructive_questions.Name: CQ9.2
constructive_questions.Details: Is Americanisation the same as globalisation? What is the role of the internet in the process of Americanisation?

constructive_questions.Name: CQ9.3
constructive_questions.Details: Looking around you, what are the influences of American culture?

constructive_questions.Name: CQ10.1
constructive_questions.Details: Explore the impact of specific areas of American popular culture like music, Hollywood, television in Vietnam . How have they been resisted or accommodated?

constructive_questions.Name: CQ10.2
constructive_questions.Details: English language acquisition in Vietnam is probably another form of colonization. Should your country Vietnam also adapt and apply the context of “Americanisation”? Is there a possibility that your country Vietnam loses its own identity if you keep on accepting immigrants or foreigners from different countries?

constructive_questions.Name: CQ10.3
constructive_questions.Details: What specific topics from the lessons on American studies had an effect on your judgment as a citizen, as an English major student, and as a person?

constructive_questions.Name: CQ11.1
constructive_questions.Details: What makes British culture? Compare and contrast it with American Culture

constructive_questions.Name: CQ11.2
constructive_questions.Details: Research online to find events across British politics and society, either in the year you were born, or in another year of significance. Which were the most important events of that time? Why do you think these are significant?

constructive_questions.Name: CQ11.3
constructive_questions.Details: Describe the cultural portrait of Britain in 2 periods by researching areas of cultural and artistic interest such as films, television, and poular music. Why were these events significant?

constructive_questions.Name: CQ12.1
constructive_questions.Details: What is the impact that cultural diversity has had and will have on the inhabitants of the United Kingdom? How such cultural diversity has complicated an effort to define “Britishness”?

constructive_questions.Name: CQ12.2
constructive_questions.Details: How has the gender issues transformed from the 1960's till present in the UK?

constructive_questions.Name: CQ12.3
constructive_questions.Details: What are some of the UK pop cultures in recent years? What is your opinion about them?

constructive_questions.Name: CQ13.1
constructive_questions.Details: Identify 3 different dialects in the British language and analyze their differences. What makes regional dialects of English distinctive?

constructive_questions.Name: CQ13.2
constructive_questions.Details: How do people who come from different regions of your country speak differently? What's the best way to learn a language?

constructive_questions.Name: CQ13.3
constructive_questions.Details: What is received pronunciation? What attitudes do people have towards speakers with received pronunciation?

constructive_questions.Name: CQ14.1
constructive_questions.Details: What are taboo words? What about political correctness? Give examples.

constructive_questions.Name: CQ14.2
constructive_questions.Details: Having considered some social aspects of language use in Britain, discuss the following: (1) Which is the ‘correct’ or ‘prestige’ accent? (2) What attitudes do people have towards speakers of regional accents and minority languages? (3) Are regional varieties of the national language found in advertising, the mass media and certain types of role in ﬁlms and plays, and what connotations do they carry?

constructive_questions.Name: CQ14.3
constructive_questions.Details: If your ﬁrst language is not English, how has that language been affected by English in recent years? Is diversity and change good for a language? What are the possible advantages and disadvantages?

constructive_questions.Name: CQ15.1
constructive_questions.Details: Why has there been a decline in British newspaper sales? What do you know about British newspapers?

constructive_questions.Name: CQ15.2
constructive_questions.Details: What were the popular pioneers of British newspapers? What impacts have British newspapers had on British society?

constructive_questions.Name: CQ15.3
constructive_questions.Details: How do British newspapers differ from each other?

constructive_questions.Name: CQ16.1
constructive_questions.Details: Why have British magazine sales been in decline despite some stories of current success?

constructive_questions.Name: CQ16.2
constructive_questions.Details: What is the main difference between Women and Men's magazines? What are popular British magazines?

constructive_questions.Name: CQ16.3
constructive_questions.Details: How have British magazines reflected social changes?

constructive_questions.Name: CQ17.1
constructive_questions.Details: Research and describe some interesting information about these British groups: 1. The Beatles 2. Queen 3. Spice Girls 4. One Direction. How have they influenced Bristish and global music?

constructive_questions.Name: CQ17.2
constructive_questions.Details: Which performers and movements do you consider the most interesting/significant in British pop since the 1960s, and why?

constructive_questions.Name: CQ17.3
constructive_questions.Details: Choose a song or album of a British band or singer with which you are familiar. If you were a critic for a music magazine read by teenagers, how would you write a review for the song/album?

constructive_questions.Name: CQ18.1
constructive_questions.Details: What are teds/mods/skinheads/hippies/punks/raves/subcultures? What are their respective tastes in music and/or fashion?

constructive_questions.Name: CQ18.2
constructive_questions.Details: How has British fashion style changed in the last two decades?

constructive_questions.Name: CQ18.3
constructive_questions.Details: In your opinion, which is the best decade for British fashion style?

constructive_questions.Name: CQ19.1
constructive_questions.Details: _ Why is cultural heritage important? How has exhibition of heritage changed these days? How do you like/dislike the way it is now?

constructive_questions.Name: CQ19.2
constructive_questions.Details: _ What are the two heritage organizations in the UK? In what way are they similar or different? How important are they to the conservation of the UK cultural heritage?

constructive_questions.Name: CQ19.3
constructive_questions.Details: Blue Plaques are permanent signs installed in a public place in the UK to link that location with a historical marker. What suggestions would you recommend to honor Vietnamese notable figures of the past and the buildings in which they lived and worked?

constructive_questions.Name: CQ20.1
constructive_questions.Details: Why was the contryside refered to as "a kind of rural dream" in the 19th century in Britain? How is it reflected in British literature and other aspects of British life?

constructive_questions.Name: CQ20.2
constructive_questions.Details: Why were English country houses (stately homes) presented as one of the great icons of British culture? Why is there a need to reconceptualize country houses for new audiences in the 21st century?

constructive_questions.Name: CQ20.3
constructive_questions.Details: How have British music festivals been globalized and commercialized? How do you like/dislike the way they are now?
